# Results — Study 681 (Relative-Rotation-Graph)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Julius de
Kempenaer's **Relative Rotation Graph**: plot each sector's **RS-Ratio** (relative-strength
level vs SPY) against its **RS-Momentum** (rate of change of that level); buy sectors in the
**Leading** quadrant, avoid **Lagging** ones, and the two-axis read should beat a plain
one-dimensional momentum rank. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `27323464af92`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes, **11 SPDR sector ETFs + SPY** (6,936 rows), 1998-12-01 → 2026-06-30 |
| Universe quirk (named) | the 9 original sector SPDRs launch 1998-12-16; **XLRE** launches 2015-10-08; **XLC** launches 2018-06-19 — same table and quirk as siblings [225-sector-rotation](../225-sector-rotation/) / [506-industry-momentum](../506-industry-momentum/) |
| RRG construction | RS-Ratio = 100 + rolling z-score(price_sector / price_SPY, **W=63** trading days); RS-Momentum = 100 + rolling z-score(RS-Ratio's **M=21**-day change, W=63) — our own explicit construction (see [`relative_rotation_graph/strategy.py`](../relative_rotation_graph/strategy.py); RRG vendors don't publish their exact smoothing constants) |
| Monthly panel | quadrant snapshot: **324 months**, 1999-07 → 2026-06 × 11 tickers; returns panel: **331 months**, 1998-12 → 2026-06 |
| Execution / costs | **one lag**: quadrant read at month-end close *t*, position held over month *t+1* (no look-ahead); one-way cost × NAV per leg (5/10/20 bps swept), round trip = 2 × one-way × realised turnover |
| Statistics | Newey-West HAC *t* on every active-return series; a **matched-random control** (Monte-Carlo, 200 seeds) picks the same number of random sectors RRG held each month (incl. cash months) to isolate *selection* skill from the mechanical cash-timing drag |

No survivorship on the Signal axis: all 11 tickers are still-listed, currently-traded ETFs used
throughout their own history (no delisted-name substitution); XLRE/XLC's shorter live history is
named above, not hidden.

## The headline — RRG "long the Leading quadrant" vs three controls (5 bps one-way cost)

| strategy | ann. return | ann. vol | Sharpe | max drawdown | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **RRG (Leading quadrant)** | **+6.66%** | 16.49% | **0.404** | −46.21% | **+2.36** |
| Equal-weight sector basket | +9.64% | 14.60% | 0.660 | −49.12% | +3.55 |
| SPY buy-and-hold | +9.46% | 15.11% | 0.626 | −50.78% | +3.25 |
| Plain 6-1 top-3 momentum | +8.45% | 13.66% | 0.619 | −32.45% | +3.36 |

RRG earns a real (t > 2) *absolute* return — but it is the **worst** Sharpe of the four books, on
the **worst** drawdown of the three long-only benchmarks. Being long equities pays; the quadrant
overlay does not add to it.

## Holdings & turnover — a busy strategy

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| mean sectors held (of 11) | **2.60** |
| months with zero sectors Leading (all-cash) | **26 / 331 (7.9%)** |
| mean one-way monthly turnover | **76.9%** |

The rule rebalances hard: on a typical month roughly three-quarters of the book's notional
turns over — the two-axis quadrant read is noisy month to month even though each axis is a
63-day rolling smooth.

## Active return — does the rotation beat each control? (Newey-West *t*)

| comparison | active ann. return | NW *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| RRG − equal-weight basket | **−2.96%/yr** | **−2.07** | 330 |
| RRG − SPY | −2.78%/yr | −1.68 | 330 |
| RRG − plain 6-1 momentum | −1.80%/yr | −0.93 | 331 |
| RRG − matched-random control (200 seeds) | **−0.50%/yr** | **−0.35** | 331 |

Two readings, and they agree: (1) vs the naive equal-weight basket the underperformance is
**itself certified** (*t* = −2.07) — the rotation is a statistically real *drag*, not a real edge, in
the wrong direction from the claim; (2) once you control for **how many** sectors RRG held each
month (including its cash months) via the matched-random control, the *selection* itself is
statistically indistinguishable from picking names blindly (*t* = −0.35). The quadrant chart does
not know which sectors to buy any better than a coin. It does not beat the one-dimensional 6-1
momentum sort it claims to improve on either (*t* = −0.93, negative point estimate).

## Cost sweep — turnover this high erodes even the absolute-return significance

| one-way cost | net ann. return | net Sharpe | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +7.58% | 0.460 | +2.69 |
| 5 bps | +6.66% | 0.404 | +2.36 |
| 10 bps | +5.74% | 0.348 | +2.03 |
| 20 bps | +3.89% | 0.236 | +1.38 |

At 77% monthly one-way turnover, realistic sector-ETF costs (a few bps at typical size, more
under stress or size) are consequential — by 20 bps one-way the absolute *t* itself drops below
the desk's bar. And recall: the absolute return was never the honest test — it's equity beta from
being long sectors most months, not stock-picking skill.

## Sub-period stability — RRG trails the naive basket in the two most recent decades

| period | RRG ann. | RRG Sharpe | RRG NW *t* | EW ann. | EW Sharpe | EW NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1999–2009 | +3.81% | 0.218 | +0.72 | +3.77% | 0.242 | +0.68 |
| 2010–2019 | +8.82% | 0.711 | +2.58 | **+12.51%** | **1.044** | **+4.30** |
| 2020–2026 | +8.52% | 0.412 | +1.21 | **+13.32%** | **0.808** | **+2.65** |

RRG roughly *ties* the naive basket in its first eleven years, then **trails it by 3.7 and
4.8 points a year** in the two decades since — exactly when sector ETFs became liquid, cheap and
crowded with quant flow. No period shows RRG beating equal-weight.

## Third axis (myth-check) — does the chart actually rotate clockwise?

Claimed cycle: **Leading → Weakening → Lagging → Improving → Leading**. Pooled month-to-month
quadrant transitions across all 11 tickers, 1999–2026 (3,117 transition-months, of which 2,195
actually changed quadrant):

| from \ to | Leading | Weakening | Lagging | Improving |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Leading** | 196 (stay) | **409** | 237 | 15 |
| **Weakening** | 173 | 251 (stay) | **247** | 9 |
| **Lagging** | 219 | 6 | 177 (stay) | **430** |
| **Improving** | **269** | 14 | 167 | 298 (stay) |

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| pooled clockwise share of quadrant CHANGES (excludes staying put) | **61.7%** |
| random-chance baseline (3 possible destinations) | 33.3% |
| per-quadrant clockwise share | Leading→Weakening 61.9% · Weakening→Lagging 57.6% · Lagging→Improving 65.6% · Improving→Leading 59.8% |
| rarest move from each quadrant | the *immediate reversal* (Weakening→Leading is the exception at 25.4%; the other three reversals are all ≤ 1.9%) |

The descriptive physics is real: when a sector's quadrant changes at all, it moves in the
claimed clockwise direction roughly **62% of the time** — nearly double the 33% a uniformly
random mover would score — and reversing straight back to the previous quadrant is rare in three
of the four states. **This is not evidence of a tradable edge** (it is partly mechanical: RS-Momentum
is *defined* as the smoothed rate-of-change of RS-Ratio, so an orderly progression is baked into
the construction) — but the chart's own story about *how* sectors move between quadrants holds
up descriptively, even though *which* sector to buy inside "Leading" does not predict anything.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic daily multi-sector panel, AR(1) persistent relative-drift per sector (planted via
`mom_strength`), no network. Detector = RRG net return vs the matched-random control, same test
as the real-tape headline.

| world | active *t* (RRG vs matched-random) |
|---|--:|
| null (`mom_strength=0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.30** (sd 1.11), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted persistent drift (`mom_strength=0.0015`, seed 681) | active **+15.30%/yr**, *t* = **+6.20** |

The detector stays quiet on a null world (1/20 ≈ the 5% false-positive rate you'd expect from
the *t* ≥ 2 threshold itself — not systematic over-firing) and lights up cleanly on a planted
persistent rotation. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The quadrant-selection edge is statistically indistinguishable from picking
  sectors at random of the same count (matched-random control, *t* = −0.35), does not beat the
  plain 6-1 momentum sort it claims to improve on (*t* = −0.93, negative point estimate), and its
  underperformance vs the naive equal-weight basket is itself **certified** (*t* = −2.07) — a real
  drag, not a real edge, and in the wrong direction from the claim.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** 77% one-way monthly turnover, the worst Sharpe of four books even
  gross, and a certified 3.7–4.8 pt/yr shortfall to the naive basket in the two most recent
  decades. Costs erode even the (irrelevant) absolute-return significance by 20 bps one-way.
- **"Does the chart actually rotate clockwise?" — CONFIRMED.** 62% of quadrant changes move in
  the claimed direction vs a 33% random baseline, and true one-step reversals are rare in three
  of four states. The visual metaphor is descriptively honest; it just doesn't pay.
